title: Less can be More: Relieving RAG Bottlenecks via Evidence Frontloading and Pressure-Adaptive Budgeting

visual_explainer.question: How should a RAG system change reranking depth when the reranker rather than the LLM becomes the serving bottleneck?
visual_explainer.takeaway: PACE separates evidence ordering from a pressure-controlled reranking budget; frontloading makes smaller budgets preserve more top-5 evidence under load.
visual_explainer.compared_with: Fixed D=100 reranking and training-free reordering methods under the same adaptive-budget policy.

analysis.tldr: PACE couples evidence-frontloading within a fixed candidate pool with a serving-pressure controller that changes reranking depth as reranker and LLM queues shift. Its strongest result is not generic agentic reasoning but a two-factor systems decomposition: evidence ordering preserves recall at smaller D, while pressure-adaptive D relieves queueing.
analysis.problem: Reranking can become the bottleneck at high arrival rates or large candidate budgets, yet reducing the reranking budget naively drops multi-hop supporting evidence.
analysis.core_idea: Greedily reorder a fixed retrieved pool using a submodular marginal-evidence-coverage objective, then choose reranking depth from relative reranker-versus-LLM serving pressure.
analysis.agent_loop: query → fixed retriever candidate pool → evidence-frontloading reorder → pressure-conditioned reranking budget D(q) → rerank → top-5 context → answer
analysis.retrieval_design: The controller changes how many already-retrieved candidates enter reranking; it does not acquire new documents. Evidence-frontloading and runtime budget selection occupy separate control surfaces.
compared_to: MMR, PRF, Dartboard, and Adaptive-K reordering/budget baselines
same pressure-adaptive budgeting policy applied across reordering methods
analysis.evidence: On HotpotQA, fixed D=100 standard dense gives complete evidence R@5 41.13, while PACE gives 62.38 at D=50 and 60.26 at D=20. In online serving at QPS=1.8, PACE uses roughly half the D=100 budget while achieving about 20% higher R@5; the same adaptive-budget policy is applied to all reordering methods, isolating the evidence-ordering advantage at comparable selected budgets.
analysis.why_it_matters: It exposes system pressure as a legitimate adaptivity signal and shows why evidence density and compute allocation should be measured separately rather than collapsed into one retrieval-budget claim.
limitations: The main online outcome is evidence recall and simulated serving latency, not end-to-end answer correctness under a matched answer model budget.
HotpotQA and 2Wiki evaluation retains only queries whose complete evidence is already in the top-100 candidate pool, so initial retrieval failure is excluded.
The pressure controller depends on the chosen reranker, generator, hardware split, arrival process, and queueing regime.
MuSiQue uses a closed candidate set and is not directly comparable to open-corpus acquisition.
